description.narrative: (Zambia): The Family Health and Nutrition mechanism will continue to provide targeted technical assistance (TA) for the GRZ Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, Adolescent, Health and Nutrition (RMNCAH&N) health services utilizing a whole province approach in Luapula and Muchinga Provinces, and also complement the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA)'s support to these services in Eastern and Southern Provinces. The demand-driven TA, will strengthen the GRZ's capacity to provide high-quality essential health care, and support public financial management and data for decision-making. It will address key factors that contribute to maternal and child deaths, including early pregnancy, weak antenatal/postnatal care, unsafe deliveries, inadequate nutrition, incomplete immunization, diarrhea, and pneumonia. FY 2022 funds will support training and mentorship in high-impact RMNCAH&N interventions; TA for service delivery; promotion of community involvement through focused training and behavior change communications; and targeted health-systems strengthening, including data analysis and data use for decision-making. This includes sustaining prevention and timely care-seeking, buffering disruptions to service delivery, and maximizing the collection, analysis and use of data to improve services. Activities will address water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) needs in health facilities to support infection prevention and control, operation and maintenance of WASH facilities and strengthening optimal hygiene behaviors among health workers and the community. Under USAID's Country Development Cooperation Strategy, the mechanism will support Development Objective 3: Capacity of Zambia's Government, Citizens and Private Sector Increased to Improve Health Outcomes and Meet Critical Needs of Vulnerable Populations and the Administration policy priority of building global health security capacity by investing in basic health care systems. .
